newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees better results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees better results in 1997.

text.p: German insurer Allianz AG said on Thursday that it expected to raise its return on equity after tax to 15 percent from 11.5 percent in the medium term.

"We are striving in the medium term to achieve an internationally competitive post-tax return in the order of 15 percent," Allianz management board chairman Henning Schulte-Noelle told the frim's sharehilder meeting.
Allianz also said it expected to see a small double-digit rise in 1997 earnings, positive underwriting and higher overall results in 1997.
Group premium income was expected to rise by 11 percent this year to 83 billion marks.
The insurer also said it planned to expand its non-insurance financial services, focusing particularly on asset management.
Schulte-Noelle told the meeting that Allainz had already for some time been offering investment funds in Italy, and was also active in this area in other countries.

He said this meant the firm had a stable platform from which to offer asset management to third parties. He said Allianz would direct its business not just towards institutional investors, but also towards private customers.
